findings.title: Optional candidate list turns an empty completed search into failure
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The demonstrated impact is bounded; no secret compromise or wrong cryptographic output is established.
findings.reproduction: Request a list for eleven abandon words plus abandon|ability (zero checksum-valid results), or ten date candidates with a wallet stub matching none.
findings.expected: Return completed counts, zero matches and no file, as the upstream CLI does.
findings.observed: The no-list controls complete. Optional serialization throws A candidate list holds 1 to 524,288 records; neither completed outcome is returned.
findings.impact: Recovery result reporting fails and work may need repeating. No invalid mnemonic is accepted.
findings.recommendedFix: Skip serialization for no retained candidates and report a clear no-file outcome.
findings.requiredVerification: Zero words/date matches, protected/unprotected lists and a non-empty positive list control.

findings.title: Stored BIP39 passphrase is validated after candidate search
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The demonstrated impact is bounded; no secret compromise or wrong cryptographic output is established.
findings.reproduction: Request an optional list for eleven abandon words plus about|zoo, stored listPassphrase of 257 ASCII bytes and a counting wallet check.
findings.expected: Reject an unrepresentable list passphrase before any search/wallet work.
findings.observed: One wallet callback runs instead of zero, then serialization correctly rejects the 256-byte limit. Upstream CLI validates the same limit before work.
findings.impact: Avoidable work and discarded completed results. Large-work exhaustion and actual PBKDF2 cost were not measured.
findings.recommendedFix: Call assertListPassphrase before searches whenever a list is requested; keep optional output failures separate from valid recovery results.
findings.requiredVerification: Words/date paths, 256/257 UTF-8 bytes, multibyte text and lone surrogates; no-list path.

findings.title: Browser SSKR Restore lacks the upstream candidate-list export
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Resolve before publishing the affected capability or workflow; the stated recovery, cleanup or release contract is not met.

evidence.method: Static installed API/UI and current upstream CLI contract comparison

findings.reproduction: Restore the two public shares of the upstream bip39-128-2-of-3 fixture and request the protected MNCL output supported by sskr-combine, including its marked-share/date-search route.
findings.expected: Optional protected original candidates with their BIP39 passphrase/order can be saved for Scanner independently of the display cap.
findings.observed: No request/result/UI list operation exists. ShareUnmasking receives no keep and its listed values are discarded. Forgotten share repair maps to sskr-export and is not a second missing-list finding.
findings.impact: Concrete CLI/browser capability gap under the workspace parity rule; no failure of valid quorum restoration is alleged.
findings.recommendedFix: Expose the upstream listed result through the existing protected candidate-list service and Restore controls.
findings.requiredVerification: One normal quorum, one small repaired-share case and bounded date candidates; decrypt/import and compare passphrase/order with CLI.

findings.title: MHFE rekey requirements omit the known wallet BIP39 passphrase
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Resolve before publishing the affected capability or workflow; the stated recovery, cleanup or release contract is not met.
findings.reproduction: Rekey an ordinary 24-word wallet with non-empty BIP39 passphrase, confirming by its address/fingerprint; choose new PIM 0 and no repair words for the clearest sentence.
findings.expected: Keep must include the independent wallet passphrase; rekeying its mnemonic does not store or replace that wallet factor.
findings.observed: Passphrase reaches confirmation, but WASM binding and native CLI both call keep/serialization with false. The browser list can say Nothing else needs to be kept: the 24 words and the password are enough.
findings.impact: Incorrect backup requirements for a known wallet factor. Default repair words avoid that exact sentence but still omit passphrase. No wallet loss or wrong recovered mnemonic was demonstrated; real emitted WASM JSON was not rerun.
findings.recommendedFix: Preserve explicit wallet-passphrase presence through upstream rekey/API/CLI results and browser instructions, including reference modes where it cannot be inferred.
findings.requiredVerification: Empty/non-empty wallet passphrases, no/default repair words, built-in/reference/owner modes and actual resulting Keep list.

findings.title: MHFE Cancel before client preparation does not prevent later work
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The demonstrated impact is bounded; no secret compromise or wrong cryptographic output is established.
findings.reproduction: Defer production engine compilation, start runCancellable, invoke its Cancel handler, then resolve compilation and a synthetic client operation.
findings.expected: Cancel latches from the start and prevents every later operation and completion.
findings.observed: The later operation starts once and resolves; cancel reaches no client (cancelled 0). Quick facts/password review stages have the same source ownership seam.
findings.impact: An operation can start after Cancel, potentially costing full Argon2 resources. No real Argon2 allocation or incorrect cipher output was demonstrated; cancellation of already active library work is a separate path.
findings.recommendedFix: Own a cancellation/revision token over preparation, every await and active work; release the shared gate.
findings.requiredVerification: Cancel during compilation, facts, password review and active operation; no late results and normal completion controls.

findings.title: Written-backup checks can publish a verdict for obsolete text
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Resolve before publishing the affected capability or workflow; the stated recovery, cleanup or release contract is not met.
findings.reproduction: Offer one original; defer its written-backup check, edit backup text or finish a newer mismatch before resolving the older synthetic success.
findings.expected: Editing or a new run invalidates the old verdict while the same original remains selected.
findings.observed: Both challenged cases append obsolete green success. Unchanged input and changing the offered original controls pass. The guard compares only the BackupCheck instance.
findings.impact: Backup reassurance can describe a different written record. Library verdicts are synthetic to isolate ordering; actual long marked-share timing/cryptography was not executed.
findings.recommendedFix: Increment an input/run revision on edits, offer and each start, and gate both success and failure.
findings.requiredVerification: Edits/dates, reverse ordering, changing original and one bounded yielding real share-check collaborator.

findings.title: Flat release omits MHFE supplemental redistribution material
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Resolve before publishing the affected capability or workflow; the stated recovery, cleanup or release contract is not met.

evidence.method: Static packager/allowlist and retained notice-text comparison

findings.reproduction: Consume an MHFE-containing flat HTML/launcher release without the source repository; inspect the legal copy loop and exact allowlist.
findings.expected: Required supplemental notices and selected Argon2 license ship as files or are merged into shipped text.
findings.observed: Only root LICENSE, ATTRIBUTION.md and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md ship. Root text references package-relative supplemental notices and LICENSE-ARGON2 absent from the allowed assets.
findings.impact: The stated redistribution-material contract is incomplete. Source checkout retains the files; this is not a legal adjudication or secret compromise. No new release bundle was built.
findings.recommendedFix: Merge supplemental material into shipped text or include explicit legal assets and update checksum/allowlist verification together.
findings.requiredVerification: Inspect one final asset set per edition for required texts, paths and SHA256SUMS; preserve upstream notices.

findings.title: Dash publication is not gated by launcher runtime acceptance
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Resolve before publishing the affected capability or workflow; the stated recovery, cleanup or release contract is not met.
findings.reproduction: A selected canonical tag has launcher tooling; Dash builds its own embedded page/executables and reaches publish.
findings.expected: The affected target executable/page starts and passes the documented launcher acceptance before publishing.
findings.observed: Publish needs resolve/release/macOS only. No launcher verifier/runtime job exists; embedding/checksum checks do not establish executable startup. Canonical release has the corresponding runtime dependency.
findings.impact: Missing acceptance gate for separately assembled Dash executables. No binary malfunction, isolation failure or failed startup was observed; no launcher/CI process was run.
findings.recommendedFix: Add Dash-profile target-runner runtime acceptance and make publishing depend on it without full Argon2 replay in routine CI.
findings.requiredVerification: Static DAG failure fixture and supported target-runner launcher/header/worker checks during release verification.

findings.title: Unbound redeemScript incorrectly selects BIP143
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The demonstrated impact is bounded; no secret compromise or wrong cryptographic output is established.
findings.reproduction: Parse a synthetic PSBTv2 with a P2PKH UTXO, unrelated 0014 witness-program redeemScript and SIGHASH_ALL. Native and correctly HASH160-bound nested SegWit controls run.
findings.expected: Contradictory metadata cannot establish witness execution; retain legacy semantics or mark context inconsistent/unknown.
findings.observed: The HASH160 relationship is separately failed, but signing analysis reports SegWit v0 / BIP143. The first failed protocol assertion prevents the later amount assertion from running; its wrong Committed description is source-derived.
findings.impact: Incorrect signature-commitment explanation for an untrusted PSBT. The inspector does not sign/broadcast and visibly reports the relationship failure. No consensus bypass or unauthorized signature is established.
findings.recommendedFix: Derive protocol from the supplied UTXO and validated script commitments; never promote from unbound optional metadata.
findings.requiredVerification: Legacy, native and nested witness controls, mismatched HASH160, conflicting UTXOs and missing context.

findings.title: PSBTv2 required locktime is described as active with all-final sequences
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The demonstrated impact is bounded; no secret compromise or wrong cryptographic output is established.
findings.reproduction: One-input PSBTv2: required height 100, sequence omitted. A non-final 0xfffffffe control uses the same required locktime.
findings.expected: Calculate nLockTime under BIP370, then explain that all-final sequences disable it.
findings.observed: Output says Effective transaction lock: block height 100. The required-locktime branch returns before the final-sequence check. Non-final control passes.
findings.impact: Misleading transaction-finality advice. Serialized locktime is not itself incorrect; no script execution, signing or broadcast was performed.
findings.recommendedFix: Apply the transaction-wide sequence-activity check after determining every locktime source.
findings.requiredVerification: Height/time/fallback locktimes with omitted/final/non-final sequences and compatible/incompatible alternatives.

findings.title: BIP85 completion restores a cleared child secret
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Resolve before publishing the affected capability or workflow; the stated recovery, cleanup or release contract is not met.
findings.reproduction: Start BIP85 with the public zero-entropy BIP39 parent; Clear while deriveBip85 is pending, then complete the earlier worker response or error. The real installer/reset are evaluated with a deferred synthetic worker.
findings.expected: Clear invalidates the whole request, terminates its worker and leaves child output and recovery reference absent.
findings.observed: Late success restores the child DOM value/result/reference. A late error is also published. Normal completion, seed wiping and final worker release controls pass; termination does not occur at reset.
findings.impact: A previous child secret remains available after the parent was discarded. Main Clear closes the feature tab, so immediate visible exposure is not claimed. No wrong BIP85 math, parent restoration or egress is demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Own the active worker and revision; invalidate/terminate on reset or parent change and gate every completion/error.
findings.requiredVerification: Clear and parent edits before readiness and replies; reverse response order; positive completion and buffer cleanup controls.

findings.title: Scanner file-read completion reinstalls a cleared candidate list
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Resolve before publishing the affected capability or workflow; the stated recovery, cleanup or release contract is not met.
findings.reproduction: Open a one-record MNCL age file encrypted to the actual importer recipient. Defer File.arrayBuffer, call panel.clear, then release file bytes. The unchanged file-open control also runs.
findings.expected: Clear invalidates the file-read stage as well as the decrypt stage; no candidate source returns.
findings.observed: The panel starts a new importer generation after the earlier Clear and exposes count 1 instead of 0. The importer-level Clear-during-decryption control now passes after Claude changes.
findings.impact: A discarded secret candidate list can become the next scan source. This is one import ownership defect with a partially corrected later stage, not an age authentication failure or demonstrated external disclosure.
findings.recommendedFix: Capture a panel revision before reading the file; invalidate it on Clear, file changes and replacement; gate open/results/errors and wipe owned buffers in finally.
findings.requiredVerification: Deferred file read and decrypt, replacement ordering, Clear and failure; unchanged encrypted import with passphrase/order controls.

findings.title: Dash dependency build inherits publication and OIDC permissions
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Resolve before publishing the affected capability or workflow; the stated recovery, cleanup or release contract is not met.
findings.reproduction: A stable canonical release is selected and the Dash release build job installs/runs the canonical build and launcher scripts.
findings.expected: Dependency-executing build jobs are read-only; write, OIDC and attestation permissions belong only to publication.
findings.observed: Workflow defaults grant contents/write, id-token/write and attestations/write. jobs.release has no override; resolve and macOS do. The canonical workflow already separates these privileges.
findings.impact: Unnecessary privileged identity is available during build execution. Abuse requires code execution there; no token theft, compromised dependency or unauthorized publication was demonstrated. Organization policy was not inspected.
findings.recommendedFix: Use read-only workflow permissions and grant publication permissions explicitly to publish.
findings.requiredVerification: Static permission assertions for every job; no CI dispatch or credential extraction is required.

findings.title: Known source-map-js advisory remains in the development lockfile
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The demonstrated impact is bounded; no secret compromise or wrong cryptographic output is established.

evidence.method: Registry advisory plus locked/installed dependency trace

findings.reproduction: Run pnpm audit --json against the locked inventory. source-map-js 1.2.1 occurs via Vitest/Vite/PostCSS.
findings.expected: The supported developer dependency graph uses a patched source-map-js version.
findings.observed: One upstream High advisory GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q / CVE-2026-93749 is reported; patched version is 1.2.2. Both affected paths are explicitly dev-only. The installed declared production closure has 27 packages and excludes this module.
findings.impact: Malicious indexed source maps can synchronously block the affected developer tooling. Project severity is medium because production inclusion and an attacker-controlled invocation path were not established. No exploit or event-loop stall was run; this is not a browser wallet secret compromise.
findings.recommendedFix: In separate remediation refresh the compatible transitive pin to 1.2.2 or later patched release and review lock/integrity changes.
findings.requiredVerification: Repeat the advisory inventory and nearest affected tooling check; do not suppress the advisory.

findings.title: MHFE Check verdict is not bound to its current fields
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Resolve before publishing the affected capability or workflow; the stated recovery, cleanup or release contract is not met.
findings.reproduction: Check A/reference F; edit container/reference to B/G during its deferred response or after the successful synthetic verdict.

findings.title: Cancelling MHFE owner confirmation retains its phrase and listener
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The demonstrated impact is bounded; no secret compromise or wrong cryptographic output is established.
findings.reproduction: The actual Rekey owner callback displays a public phrase; cancel or fail the synthetic outer client operation before answering.
findings.expected: Every exit empties the textarea, removes its blur listener and settles/disposes the question.
findings.observed: Cancel/failure remove DOM but retain its value/listener and pending question; dispatched blur still touches the detached node. Normal No-answer cleanup passes; gate/Cancel cleanup pass.
findings.impact: Unnecessary live phrase retention and accumulating listeners until page disposal. No external leak or new attacker access is established; this is distinct from immutable-string erasure limitations.
findings.recommendedFix: Use one idempotent disposable owner-prompt cleanup for answer, cancellation, failure, replacement and teardown.
findings.requiredVerification: Answer/Cancel/failure/replacement paths, detached-value clearing, listener removal, promise settlement and gate controls.

findings.title: Password review choices reappear after the password was cleared
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The demonstrated impact is bounded; no secret compromise or wrong cryptographic output is established.
findings.reproduction: Defer PasswordReview.choose, clear/edit its field and emit the actual input event, then complete the old synthetic review.
findings.expected: The obsolete review remains hidden/empty and cannot retain or publish its password answers.
findings.observed: The reset occurs, but the response restores a visible box with three initially concealed choices. The next choose has a pending-text equality check.
findings.impact: Stale secret-bearing UI choices can be explicitly revealed after clearing. No automatic reveal, wrong-password operation or external disclosure is established; coordinator rates bounded presentation impact low.
findings.recommendedFix: Capture revisions of both repeated fields and drop obsolete review results/continuations.
findings.requiredVerification: Edit either field, reverse overlapping reviews, concealed-state cleanup and unchanged-input control.

limitations: All findings remain open; no product fixes performed. Controlled VM probes use unchanged production owners with synthetic collaborators, not native-browser cryptographic acceptance.
No full-cost MHFE operation or source-to-WASM reproduction. Local vendor/producers/hashes establish identity only.

Owner supplied a narrative claiming full-cost MHFE and launcher/486-test checks; these are contextual claims without independently retained command/source binding and are not credited as new audit passes.
Both vendors explicitly declare unreleased dirty working-tree inputs; local provenance warns and CI is expected to reject. Replace with published verified releases before release acceptance.

Initial restricted-network GitHub availability checks were 0/10; the final network-enabled check verified 10/10 public base commits. That does not verify uncommitted imported bytes as signed releases. No Cargo advisory inventory or exhaustive transitive-code audit.
Not every UI, format width, share quorum, provider/proof, export schema, viewport or feature combination was executed. Remaining scoped CHECK gaps are explicit.
Minor mobile MnemoCode tab-label crowding needs focused usability follow-up; no claim of full accessibility acceptance.
Decode completed-result invalidation/date listeners, Split revision/settings ownership and QR/import ordering remain follow-ups, not accepted unproven findings.
Sampling cannot guarantee machine-wide memory use between samples or constrain unrelated desktop tasks. All measured audit peaks stayed under 14 GiB.
No demonstrated direct secret exfiltration, unauthorized spending or wrong key/address in executed bounded vectors; absence of those observations is not proof of exhaustive safety.
